title: Clustering, step by step
sub: k-means alternates two simple steps; DBSCAN grows clusters through dense regions.

frames.caption: 120 unlabelled points. k-means with k = 3 starts with three centroids placed badly on purpose.
Iteration 1, assign: every point joins its nearest centroid.
Iteration 1, update: move each centroid to the mean of its points.
Iteration 2, assign: every point joins its nearest centroid.
Iteration 2, update: move each centroid to the mean of its points.
Iteration 3, assign: every point joins its nearest centroid.

Iteration 4, assign: every point joins its nearest centroid.
Iteration 4, update: move each centroid to the mean of its points.
Assignments didn't change: converged. Three clean groups, each centroid at its group's mean.
Two interlocking half-moons. Run k-means with k = 2.
Iteration 1, assign: every point joins its nearest centroid.
Iteration 1, update: move each centroid to the mean of its points.
Iteration 2, assign: every point joins its nearest centroid.
Iteration 2, update: move each centroid to the mean of its points.

Converged, and wrong: k-means sliced across the moons (only 72% of points land in their own moon's cluster). It can only draw straight boundaries between centroids, so it always makes convex, roughly round clusters.
DBSCAN instead: a point is a core point if at least 4 points lie within radius 0.5 of it. Clusters grow by hopping from core point to core point.

Each moon is one cluster (100% match), found without telling DBSCAN how many clusters to look for. Points in sparse areas would be labelled noise (gray). The trade-off: you must choose the radius and density threshold instead.
